B02_ZONE_BATTCONN.label: Zone: Battery Connector

B02_ZONE_IFC.label: Zone: IF Connector
B02_ZONE_IFC.note: The IFC sits a short distance in from the port. Between the port and the mainboard sits a connection most people never think about.

B02_ZONE_PMIC.label: Zone: Charger IC (PMIC)
B02_ZONE_PMIC.note: Mid-board, under a shield can. Smaller than a fingernail and the safety guard of the entire charging path.

B02_ZONE_PORT.label: Zone: Charging Port
B02_ZONE_PORT.note: The charging port sits at the board EDGE - the only part of the whole charging path exposed to the outside world, and the single most common source of charging complaints.

B02_MAINBOARD.label: Mainboard Assembly
B02_MAINBOARD.note: The whole board. Trace the path with a finger: port, IF connector, Charger IC, battery connector.

B28_BASE.label: Hot Air Rework Station
B28_BASE.note: A controlled-temperature heat gun used to desolder or reflow small parts - connectors, ports, chips - without a fixed contact tip.

B28_CRADLE.label: Handpiece Cradle
B28_CRADLE.note: The handpiece has a home. Always return it to the stand - never leave it resting on the bench.

B28_CRADLE_YOKE.label: Handpiece Cradle
B28_CRADLE_YOKE.note: The handpiece has a home. Always return it to the stand - never leave it resting on the bench.

B28_DISPLAY.label: Temperature / Airflow Display
B28_DISPLAY.note: Blank by design - the runtime draws the number, because it changes per procedure step. Fixes 2 and 3 call for 380-450 C.

B28_AIRFLOW.label: Airflow Cone
B28_AIRFLOW.note: Shows that hot air affects an AREA, not a point - which is exactly why the heat-resistant tape shielding in Fixes 4, 5 and 6 is necessary rather than fussy.

B28_NOZZLE_3mm.label: Nozzle (3mm)
B28_NOZZLE_3mm.note: Directs the hot air. Hold the nozzle at least 5 mm away from the board, and heat evenly - never pry a cold part off.

B28_NOZZLE_5mm.label: Nozzle (5mm)
B28_NOZZLE_5mm.note: Directs the hot air. Hold the nozzle at least 5 mm away from the board, and heat evenly - never pry a cold part off.

B28_NOZZLE_8mm.label: Nozzle (8mm)
B28_NOZZLE_8mm.note: Directs the hot air. Hold the nozzle at least 5 mm away from the board, and heat evenly - never pry a cold part off.

B28_NOZZLE_COLLAR.label: Nozzle Collar
B28_NOZZLE_COLLAR.note: Where nozzles swap. 3, 5 and 8 mm nozzles are available.

B28_NOZZLE_GLOW.label: Nozzle Throat
B28_NOZZLE_GLOW.note: Glows with set temperature. The straw-to-blue discolouration on the tip tells you this end is HOT without any label.

B28_STANDOFF_5MM.label: 5 mm Standoff Guide
B28_STANDOFF_5MM.note: Toggle this on to teach the safe working distance.

B28_HANDPIECE.label: Hot Air Handpiece
B28_HANDPIECE.note: The gun itself. This is what the learner aims.

B28_KNOB_AIR.label: Airflow Knob
B28_KNOB_AIR.note: Sets air volume. Too much airflow blows small neighbouring parts off the board.

B28_KNOB_TEMP.label: Temperature Knob
B28_KNOB_TEMP.note: Sets the air temperature. Too hot tears pads; too cold and you pry a part off cold.

ASM_FLEX_FILM.label: Flex Cable (in situ)
ASM_FLEX_FILM.note: The flex as it actually sits on the board, spanning the 14.8 mm gap from port to socket.

B11_BODY_BACK.label: Board-Side Receptacle (Socket)
B11_BODY_BACK.note: The small connector soldered onto the mainboard that the flex cable plugs into.

B11_BODY_END_L.label: Board-Side Receptacle (Socket)
B11_BODY_END_L.note: The small connector soldered onto the mainboard that the flex cable plugs into.

B11_BODY_END_R.label: Board-Side Receptacle (Socket)
B11_BODY_END_R.note: The small connector soldered onto the mainboard that the flex cable plugs into.

B11_BODY_FLOOR.label: Board-Side Receptacle (Socket)
B11_BODY_FLOOR.note: The small connector soldered onto the mainboard that the flex cable plugs into.

B11_FLAP_LIP.label: Flap Leading Edge
B11_FLAP_LIP.note: The lip on the flap's front edge. If the flap is only part-closed, the gap shows here.

B11_FLAP.label: Locking Latch / ZIF Flap
B11_FLAP.note: A small hinged flap that clamps the flex in place after insertion (Zero Insertion Force - it needs no force to insert, only to lock). If left loose or unlatched, this causes intermittent charging: the phone charges only if you hold the cable at just the right angle. One of the most misdiagnosed faults in the whole course.

B05_PIN_A05.label: Pin A5 - CC1

B05_PIN_A06.label: Pin A6 - D+

B05_PIN_B05.label: Pin B5 - CC2

B05_PIN_B06.label: Pin B6 - D+
B05_PIN_B06.note: Legacy USB 2.0 data line - data transfer and, on many phones, basic charger-type detection.

B05_PIN_B07.label: Pin B7 - D-
B05_PIN_B07.note: Legacy USB 2.0 data line - data transfer and, on many phones, basic charger-type detection.

B05_PIN_B08.label: Pin B8 - SBU2
B05_PIN_B08.note: Sideband Use. Reserved for alternate modes - audio out, video out (DisplayPort/HDMI over USB-C).

B05_PIN_B09.label: Pin B9 - VBUS
B05_PIN_B09.note: Carries the actual power (voltage) coming in from the charger cable.

B05_PIN_B10.label: Pin B10 - RX1-
B05_PIN_B10.note: SuperSpeed data pair (USB 3.x). Not used for basic charging.

B05_PIN_B11.label: Pin B11 - RX1+
B05_PIN_B11.note: SuperSpeed data pair (USB 3.x). Not used for basic charging.

B05_PIN_B12.label: Pin B12 - GND
B05_PIN_B12.note: Ground return path - completes the circuit back to the charger.

B05_SHELL.label: Metal Shell (Shield)
B05_SHELL.note: Outer metal casing around the port. Grounds the connector and blocks electromagnetic interference. Often the first thing to bend or crack on port-drop damage.

B05_SHELL_SEAM.label: Shell Fold Seam
B05_SHELL_SEAM.note: The draw line where the stamped shell is formed.

B05_SHELL_TAB_L.label: Shield / Ground Tab
B05_SHELL_TAB_L.note: Anchors the port to the board. A broken shield tab is a very common 'not charging' cause - and these are soldered FIRST when fitting a new port.

B05_SHELL_TAB_R.label: Shield / Ground Tab
B05_SHELL_TAB_R.note: Anchors the port to the board. A broken shield tab is a very common 'not charging' cause - and these are soldered FIRST when fitting a new port.

B05_TONGUE.label: Contact Tongue
B05_TONGUE.note: The blade the 24 contacts sit on. Light-coloured plastic on purpose, so the gold contacts stand out.

B05_PORT.label: USB-C Charging Port
B05_PORT.note: The charging port looks like a simple slot - but inside there is a small city of pins. Opening is 8.34 x 2.56 mm, 6.20 mm deep.

B02_ZONE_BATTCONN.label: Zone: Battery Connector

B02_ZONE_IFC.label: Zone: IF Connector

B02_ZONE_PMIC.label: Zone: Charger IC (PMIC)

B02_ZONE_PORT.label: Zone: Charging Port
B02_ZONE_PORT.note: The charging port sits at the board EDGE - the only part of the whole charging path exposed to the outside world, and the single most common source of charging complaints.

B02_MAINBOARD.label: Mainboard Assembly
B02_MAINBOARD.note: The whole board. Trace the path with a finger: port, IF connector, Charger IC, battery connector.

B11_LATCH.teaching: HALF_CLOSED looks closed but is not. It is the 'charges only at one angle' fault.

notes: Materials are SHARED. Changing MAT_PIN_VBUS lights all four VBUS pins at once - correct for signal-group teaching. Per-pin highlighting needs material.clone() first.
Every state ships VISIBLE because glTF has no per-node visibility. Hide all but the default on load, or all five B40 joints render on top of each other.
glTF carries no animated material properties. Solder glow and nozzle heat ramp must be driven runtime-side alongside the clip.
Assets are at true mm scale: 1 world unit = 1 mm. Set camera.near = 0.01 or a 9 mm connector clips at macro zoom.
